Hey, you all know how reddit has an expiration date for links? Why does voat need that? Why can't you vote on anything, regardless of how old it is?

Why can't you vote on anything, regardless of how old it is?

Have you considered Googling your query?

The reason old submissions are archived is due to technical limitations of reddit. IIRC, it done to limit the size of the database that is live/accessible on the site at any given time.

It is not a policy so much as it is an automatic function of reddit. [...]

Also, as further and further comment depths are created in a comment chain, the server processing time for the next comment goes up and it causes lag for the site as a whole. The archival system on reddit is intended to prevent those issues, not vote brigading on old posts. Back when I joined Voat, I asked @Atko if Voat could suffer a similar issue with abnormally deep comment chains, and he responded that this shouldn't be an issue given that Voat is completely different at the source code / programming language level.

In addition to the platform differences, the API is introducing a query pipeline that that produces a real-time comment tree in a light weight but dynamic way so comments can be piece meal loaded without much concern for the of depth or nesting levels.

If you can load from any point in a tree (without starting at the top and traversing) and only load 2-3 levels in an operation performance isn't a major concern.
